title: Macanese Almond Cookies
description: Pressed rather than rolled, from toasted mung bean flour rubbed with cold lard. They come out sandy and dry and dissolve on the tongue. Makes about two dozen.
notes: Mung bean flour is what gives these their particular chalky-in-a-good-way crumb; fine rice flour is the usual substitute and produces a slightly harder cookie. Lard is not negotiable if you want the texture — butter has water in it and water builds gluten.

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.note: chilled hard and cut into small cubes

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.note: half of them ground fine, half left as halves

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: only if the mix will not hold together

steps.text: Toast the mung bean flour in a dry pan over a low heat until it smells nutty and has lost its raw edge, then spread it out and let it cool completely.
steps.tip: Cool it properly before it meets the fat. Warm flour melts the lard on contact and the sandy crumb goes with it.

steps.text: Rub the chilled lard into the flour, the icing sugar and the salt with your fingertips until it looks like damp sand, adding the water a few drops at a time only if it refuses to come together.
steps.tip: Judge it by squeezing, not by looking. A handful that holds its shape when you open your fist is done; one that falls apart wants a drop more.

steps.text: Stir through the ground almonds and keep the halves back for the tops.
Pack the mixture hard into a mould or a small ring, press an almond half onto each top, and knock them out onto a lined tray.
steps.tip: Pack it far harder than feels reasonable. These are pressed, not rolled, and a loosely filled mould gives a cookie that slumps on the way to the oven.

steps.text: Bake until the edges are set and the tops have barely taken any colour.
Leave them on the tray until they are stone cold before moving a single one.
steps.tip: They only become structurally sound once cool. Lift one warm and it falls through your fingers.
